source_lines.text: **Given:** the Axiom of Choice; a coefficient field $k$; a smooth complex algebraic variety $M$ of pure dimension $d$ with its analytic topology; morphisms of complex algebraic varieties $q:A\to M$ and $u:B\to M$; the fiber product $T=A\times_MB$ with its projections $a:T\to A$, $b:T\to B$; the diagonal $\Delta:M\to M\times M$; the map $F=(q,u):A\times B\to M\times M$; and the closed embedding $\theta:T\hookrightarrow A\times B$ of the support, which realizes $T$ as $F^{-1}(\Delta(M))$. For the equivariant assertions, additionally impose the characteristic-zero, product-general-linear-group and equivariance hypotheses of [F3].

2.1 Pullback and cap product on arbitrary supports. Put $S=A\times B$. Proper base change along $F=(q,u)$ identifies $F^*\Delta_*k_M[-2d]$ with $\theta_*k_T[-2d]$, so $F^*g_\Delta$ gives $g_F:\theta_*k_T[-2d]\to k_S$. For a dualizing class $c:k_S\to\omega_S[-n]$, compose $c\circ g_F$ and use $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$ and $\theta^!\omega_S=\omega_T$. The resulting map $k_T\to\omega_T[2d-n]$ is a Borel–Moore class of degree $n-2d$ on $T$. This defines the supported cap operation even if $T$ is singular or has excess dimension; no purity of $\theta$ is asserted. The external product uses $\omega_A\boxtimes\omega_B=\omega_S$: on the supplied finite local product cochain models, compact-support cochains tensor, and their finite-dimensional duals tensor as well, giving this canonical comparison and its restriction compatibility. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Comparison with the exchange mate. For a constructible $C$ on $M$, the mate is the adjoint of $b_!a^*q^!C\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^{-1}}u^*q_!q^!C\xrightarrow{u^*\epsilon_q}u^*C$, where the arbitrary-map proper-support exchange of [F1] supplies $\mathrm{BC}:u^*q_!\xrightarrow{\sim}b_!a^*$ and $\epsilon_q$ is the exceptional counit. To identify its dualizing evaluation with step 2.1, factor $q$ as its graph $\Gamma_q:A\hookrightarrow A\times M$ followed by the second projection. The graph is the pullback of $\Delta$ along $(q,\operatorname{id}_M):A\times M\to M\times M$; its supported orientation map is that pullback of $g_\Delta$. Base change of the graph along $\operatorname{id}_A\times u$ is exactly $\theta$, so its supported orientation map after this second pullback is $g_F$. For the product projection, tensor–Hom evaluation with the relative dualizing factor $\omega_A$ computes the counit; this is the finite product cochain evaluation of step 2.1. Composing the graph counit and that evaluation gives $\epsilon_q$ by the composition-of-counits identity in [F1]. Cartesian pasting therefore makes its base-changed composite exactly $u^*\epsilon_q\circ\mathrm{BC}^{-1}$ above. Taking adjoints and using $q^!k_M=\omega_A[-2d]$ proves that the exchange, paired with the second dualizing class by tensor evaluation, is $c\circ g_F$ under $\theta_*\dashv\theta^!$. Every map retains support on $T$ throughout this factorization. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1]

candidates.source_claim: The support T=A×_M B is identified with F^{-1}(Δ(M)) for F=(q,u), and the proof identifies the supported exchange mate by factoring q through its graph and pulling back to θ:T↪A×B.

candidates.why_warranted: The proof tracks the same support through a fiber-product square, the diagonal pullback, and a second graph-base-change square. A compact diagram can make the domains, projections, and identification of θ easier to follow.

Draw F=(q,u):A×B→M×M and Δ:M↪M×M, with θ:T↪A×B identified as the Cartesian pullback F^{-1}(Δ(M)).
For the exchange factorization, draw Γ_q:A↪A×M followed by the second projection A×M→M, and the base-change square of Γ_q along id_A×u:A×B→A×M whose pullback is θ.
Annotate the induced support maps g_Δ, g_F, and that support remains on T through the exchange-mate comparison.
mathematical_checks: Check that the first square is Cartesian precisely because F∘θ=Δ∘(q∘a)=Δ∘(u∘b).
Check that the graph Γ_q is the pullback of Δ along (q,id_M):A×M→M×M.
Check that the pullback of Γ_q along id_A×u is T=A×_M B, with the correct projection maps and θ codomain A×B.
Keep the diagram explanatory; do not use it as a proof of the supported orientation, exchange mate, or counit identities.

source_lines.text: Work in the normalization of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]], write permutations in one-line notation, and put $q=v^{-2}$ as in [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]. (a) In $S_2$: $r_{\mathrm{id},21}=v-v^{-1}$, $\underline H_{\mathrm{id}}=H_{\mathrm{id}}$, $\underline H_{21}=H_{21}+vH_{\mathrm{id}}$, $P_{\mathrm{id},21}(q)=1$, $\mu(\mathrm{id},21)=1$ and $\underline H_{21}^2=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_{21}$. (b) In $S_3$ the bar images of the standard basis are $$\overline{H_{132}}=H_{132}+(v-v^{-1})H_{123},\qquad \overline{H_{213}}=H_{213}+(v-v^{-1})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{231}}=H_{231}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{312}}=H_{312}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})H_{123},$$ $$\overline{H_{321}}=H_{321}+(v-v^{-1})(H_{231}+H_{312})+(v^2-2+v^{-2})(H_{132}+H_{213})+(v^3-2v+2v^{-1}-v^{-3})H_{123},$$ the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis is $$\underline H_{123}=H_{123},\quad \underline H_{132}=H_{132}+vH_{123},\quad \underline H_{213}=H_{213}+vH_{123},$$ $$\underline H_{231}=H_{231}+v(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^2H_{123},\quad \underline H_{312}=H_{312}+v(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^2H_{123},$$ $$\underline H_{321}=H_{321}+v(H_{231}+H_{312})+v^2(H_{132}+H_{213})+v^3H_{123},$$ all $P_{y,w}(q)$ with $y\le w$ equal $1$, and $\mu(y,w)=1$ exactly when $y\lessdot w$ is a cover of the Bruhat order on $S_3$ (the eight covers $(123,132)$, $(123,213)$, $(132,231)$, $(132,312)$, $(213,231)$, $(213,312)$, $(231,321)$, $(312,321)$ in one-line notation). (c) Multiplication checks: $\underline H_{21}^2=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_{21}$ and, in the case $sw>w$ with one $\mu$-edge, $\underline H_{132}\underline H_{231}=\underline H_{321}+\underline H_{132}$ (here $s_2\cdot 231=321$ and $s_2\cdot 132=123<132$, so the sum in [[thm-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-multiplication-formula]] has the single term $\mu(132,231)=1$).

2.1 **Polynomials and covers.** Reading the expansions in step 1.3 gives $p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}$ for every $y\le w$, so [F4] gives $P_{y,w}=1$ and $\mu(y,w)=[v]p_{y,w}$ is $1$ exactly at length difference one. By the reduced-subword criterion [F6], the Bruhat ranks in $S_3$ are $\{123\}$, $\{132,213\}$, $\{231,312\}$, and $\{321\}$, and each element in one of these layers is below every element in the next layer. Hence the covers are precisely the two edges from $123$, the four edges from rank one to rank two, and the two edges into $321$; these are exactly the eight pairs listed. Grading rules out other covers. [F4, F6, step 1.3, algebra]

candidates.source_claim: The example states that the four Bruhat ranks are {123}, {132,213}, {231,312}, {321}, with every element in one rank below every element in the next, and lists the eight cover pairs; the Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient μ(y,w) is 1 exactly on those covers.
candidates.diagram_kind: Bruhat Hasse diagram for S₃, with permutations in one-line notation
candidates.why_warranted: The example compresses the entire S₃ Bruhat cover structure into a long formula and repeated list of eight pairs. A small Hasse diagram would let readers see and check the cover support at a glance.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: Place 123 in rank 0; 132 and 213 in rank 1; 231 and 312 in rank 2; and 321 in rank 3.
Use the same one-line permutation labels and composition convention stated in the item; optionally mark μ(y,w)=1 on each edge.
mathematical_checks: Verify each listed arrow is a Bruhat cover under the reduced-subword convention and has inversion-length increase one.
Verify the diagram has exactly eight edges and no additional comparabilities are drawn as covers.
Check arrow orientation is from lower to higher Bruhat order and that the rank layers match the source.
